\[
\boxed{\left(a,b\right)=\left(\frac1{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}},\ \frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}\right)}
\]

Let
\[
\phi=\frac{\pi}{2n},\qquad c=\cos\phi,\qquad s=\sin\phi.
\]

First, for any admissible pair \((a,b)\), take
\[
\theta_0=\pi-\phi.
\]
Then
\[
\cos\theta_0=-c,
\]
and
\[
\cos(n\theta_0)=\cos\left(n\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0.
\]
So nonnegativity gives
\[
0\le P_{a,b}(\theta_0)=1+2a(-c)=1-2ac.
\]
Hence
\[
a\le \frac1{2c}=\frac1{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}}.
\]

It remains to show this upper bound is attainable. Set
\[
a=\frac1{2c},\qquad b=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\phi.
\]
Then
\[
P_{a,b}(\theta)=1+\frac{\cos\theta}{c}+\frac{(-1)^n s}{nc}\cos(n\theta),
\]
so
\[
cP_{a,b}(\theta)=c+\cos\theta+\frac{(-1)^n s}{n}\cos(n\theta).
\]

Write \(\theta=\pi-u\), with \(u\in[0,\pi]\). Then
\[
\cos\theta=-\cos u,\qquad \cos(n\theta)=(-1)^n\cos(nu),
\]
so
\[
cP_{a,b}(\theta)=h(u):=c-\cos u+\frac{s}{n}\cos(nu).
\]

We prove \(h(u)\ge0\). Its derivative is
\[
h'(u)=\sin u-s\sin(nu).
\]

For \(0\le u\le\phi\), one has \(\sin u\le s\sin(nu)\), so \(h'(u)\le0\). Also
\[
h(\phi)=c-c+\frac{s}{n}\cos\frac{\pi}{2}=0.
\]
Thus \(h(u)\ge0\) on \([0,\phi]\).

For \(\phi\le u\le\pi-\phi\), we have \(\sin u\ge s\) and \(\sin(nu)\le1\), hence
\[
h'(u)=\sin u-s\sin(nu)\ge0.
\]
So \(h(u)\ge h(\phi)=0\) on this interval.

Finally, for \(\pi-\phi\le u\le\pi\),
\[
c-\cos u\ge 2c,\qquad \frac{s}{n}\cos(nu)\ge-\frac{s}{n},
\]
so
\[
h(u)\ge 2c-\frac{s}{n}>0.
\]
Therefore \(P_{a,b}(\theta)\ge0\) for all real \(\theta\).

Thus the largest possible value is
\[
\boxed{a_{\max}=\frac1{2\cos\frac{\pi}{2n}}},
\]
and the corresponding value of \(b\) is
\[
\boxed{b=\frac{(-1)^n}{2n}\tan\frac{\pi}{2n}}.
\]
